correctness.rationale: For a noncircular ellipse Z(w)=aw+b/w, the profile H_p(w)=p(Z(w))conj[p(Z(w))] on |w|=1 is Laurent with exponents [−2d,2d], and its extreme coefficients coincide as the real number (ab)^d|c_d|². Thus P=w^{2d}H has equal constant/leading coefficients; at 4d distinct unit nodes, Lagrange interpolation P=P0+C∏(w−w_j) forces C=P0(0)/(1−∏w_j), proving full-profile reconstruction whenever product !=1. Rational-function invariance under both Joukowski deck maps forces the quotient p/q to be constant: a nonconstant rational function cannot be invariant under dilation (b/a)². Equispaced nodes have product −e^{4diθ0}; at bad offsets generalized Chebyshev F_d(Z(w))=a^dw^d+b^dw^{-d} has intensity constant on the nodes, matching a nonzero constant polynomial. Polarization gives full real profile-space rank 4d, with no top sine harmonic. I independently checked numerical Fourier evaluation ranks d=1..4 at good/bad grid offsets, and inspected the all-degree algebraic argument. Finite checks are corroborative only.
residual_risks: The product condition is sufficient for arbitrary 4d-node phaseless injectivity, not proved necessary outside regular grids; 4d lower bound is only for *linear entire-profile* interpolation, not nonlinear coefficient recovery.
